name: Bulería (flamenco festive fast palo)
lineage: Andalusian bulería flamenco palo, the fast-tempo festive-celebratory form developed in late-nineteenth-century Jerez de la Frontera from the older soleá tradition. Characterized by the canonical twelve-beat bulería compás (accents shifted from soleá to beats 12, 3, 6, 8, 10 with characteristic rhythmic-displacement-and-suspension play), fast tempo, and improvisational-virtuosic vocal-and-guitar-and-palmas (hand-clapping) interplay. Lyric content spans humorous, romantic, and celebratory themes — much lighter than the cante jondo deep-songs. The bulería closes most flamenco performance sets as the festive-final palo. Distinguished from soleá by bulería's faster tempo, lighter emotional register, and the canonical Jerez-rhythmic-displacement-and-virtuosity practice.
